# Phase A §8/§10: generated from `requirements.in` -- do not hand-edit. Regenerate
# deliberately, on its own PR, with:
#   pip install pip-tools
#   pip-compile requirements.in
#
# This file was generated by capturing `pip freeze` from a venv where the complete test
# suite (525 tests) was passing, rather than a fresh, unverified dependency resolution --
# every version below is one that was actually exercised, not merely "latest compatible".
# Exact pins are required (not just floors) for numpy/pandas/scikit-learn/joblib in
# particular: model artifacts are joblib-pickled against a specific numpy/scikit-learn ABI,
# and an unreviewed transitive upgrade here can silently change training determinism or
# break deserialization of an already-saved artifact. Dev-only tooling (mypy, ruff,
# coverage, pip-tools and their own transitive deps) is intentionally excluded -- it was
# never part of this file and is not a runtime dependency of the application.
#
# Known, currently-unresolved issue: joblib 1.5.3 (the latest release as of this pin --
# confirmed via `pip index versions joblib`) still uses a NumPy array-shape-assignment
# pattern that NumPy 2.5 deprecates, producing a DeprecationWarning during model
# load/unpickle. This is not suppressed here (suppressing it would hide a real future
# breakage risk); it's a joblib-side fix pending upstream. Re-check `pip index versions
# joblib` when bumping this pin deliberately.
#
# catboost/contourpy/cycler/fonttools/graphviz/kiwisolver/matplotlib/pillow/plotly/pyparsing
# are transitive: catboost's own PyPI package hard-depends on matplotlib/plotly/graphviz for
# eval-visualization tooling this project never calls -- a real, accepted dependency-weight
# tradeoff (see app/ml/algorithm_registry.py), not an oversight.
#
# PyJWT[crypto] (Task: first isolated JWT/JWKS authentication vertical slice, app.core.
# jwt_auth) added deliberately for RS256 verification. cffi/cryptography/pycparser below are
# its own genuinely required transitive dependencies -- confirmed via `pip-compile
# requirements.in` resolving them from cryptography's own declared metadata (not hand-added
# or guessed), and cross-checked against a manually installed/verified environment reporting
# the exact same PyJWT==2.14.0/cryptography==50.0.1. No other pin in this file changed as a
# result of this addition -- re-verified line-by-line against the prior committed version of
# this file before restoring it to this same structure/comment set.
